route: Economic case [observed] → Strategy call [observed] → Agreement before charge [observed] → Week-one intake [observed] → Build and approval [observed] → Launch and optimization [observed]
limitations: No se enviaron formularios, no se contactó a la empresa y no se inventaron etapas posteriores al CTA.
No se detectó una firma técnica comercial reconocible en scripts, iframes, enlaces o formularios públicos; esto no demuestra que no exista.
No se enviaron formularios ni datos personales.
No se contactó con la empresa.
redVitalia: **Adaptar:** una acción principal inequívoca como “Tour the live platform demo”, manteniendo una sola ruta dominante por landing.
**Adaptar:** convertir la reversión de riesgo visible en una condición contractual medible, no en una promesa ambigua.
**Copiar con control:** presentar casos con cliente, periodo, inversión, denominador y resultado; distinguir siempre datos autodeclarados de auditoría independiente.
**Copiar:** responder objeciones de precio, plazo, permanencia y resultados antes del CTA de alto compromiso.

message.headline: One fee. The whole outbound engine.
message.promise: Replace the cost and complexity of an internal outbound team with a complete managed engine.
message.positioning: The service is sold as a complete system with people, process and platform rather than isolated appointments.
message.audience: B2B teams seeking outsourced outbound capacity · Teams comparing agency cost with an internal SDR function

fields: Date and time visible before deeper booking steps
forms.friction: No time was selected, so later questions were not observed.

funnel.detail: Pricing content compares the managed engine with building an internal team.
Visitor enters a custom 30-minute booking flow.
The public process says the people, plan and copy are approved before invoice and launch.
A Playmaker gathers ICP, offer, personas, objections, proof and domain requirements.
Lists, copy and scripts are prepared in week two for client approval.
Launch occurs around weeks two to three, with first meetings expected around weeks three to four and continuing tests.

pricing: Exact prices were not public on the reviewed page
100+, 250+ or 500+ daily touches depending on tier
contract: Outreach and billing end at the end of the next billing month
guarantee: Risk is reduced through approval before invoice and launch; no public result guarantee was observed.

objections: Paying before seeing the team and plan
Cost versus an internal SDR team
contradictions: qualification — The notice and billing timing should appear beside the cancellation claim. — Month-to-month and cancel-anytime language reduces perceived lock-in. — Written notice applies and activity ends at the end of the next billing month.

terms-scope — The signed agreement remains the controlling source. — The public process is specific about onboarding. — General website terms do not guarantee outcomes and a client agreement may supersede them.
inferences: The approval-before-invoice sequence is designed to remove fear of agency bait-and-switch. — confidence: high — basis: The process repeatedly foregrounds approval of people, plan and wording before launch.
The custom booking interface is also a live demand signal. — confidence: medium — basis: The modal displayed a recent strategy-call booking count.
notObservable: Questions after selecting a booking time
limitations: Headline performance totals were not independently audited.
No client agreement or private proposal was available.

copy: Name the owner of each onboarding step
Make the approval and billing trigger explicit
Frame the offer against the full cost of an internal alternative
avoid: Using cancel-anytime language without adjacent notice detail
Leaving package prices entirely opaque if qualification permits a range
test: A visible launch timeline with expected first-result window
